blocks.title: Key takeaways:
blocks.text: OVER() adds a column without collapsing rows; ORDER BY inside it builds the running total; the window sees the whole department. PARTITION BY restarts per group. ROW_NUMBER never ties, RANK skips after ties, DENSE_RANK does not.

lines: WITH austin AS (SELECT * FROM departments WHERE location = 'Austin')
SELECT name FROM austin ORDER BY name; -- Q49 derived table to WITH
WITH c AS (SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) n FROM employees
WHERE id <= 4 GROUP BY dept_id), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) m FROM c)
SELECT dept_id, n, n > m AS above FROM c, a ORDER BY dept_id; -- Q50 chain CTEs, compare to avg
WITH c AS (SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) n FROM employees
SELECT d.name, c.n FROM c JOIN departments d ON d.id = c.dept_id
WHERE c.n > 1; -- Q51 filter aggregate CTE (WHERE, not HAVING)
WITH RECURSIVE up AS (SELECT * FROM employees WHERE id = 2
UNION ALL SELECT e.* FROM employees e JOIN up ON e.id = up.manager_id)
SELECT name FROM up; -- Q52 chain upward (stops at NULL manager_id)
WITH RECURSIVE o AS (SELECT id, name, 1 d FROM employees
WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL
SELECT e.id, e.name, d + 1 FROM employees e JOIN o ON e.manager_id = o.id)
SELECT name, d FROM o ORDER BY d, id LIMIT 3; -- Q53 org depth (anchor 1, step +1)
WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 3)
SELECT i FROM n; -- Q54 number series (WHERE is the stop rule)
WITH r AS (SELECT employee_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) rn FROM orders)
SELECT MIN(rn) AS keep FROM r; -- Q55 latest order per employee (rn = 1 is newest)
WITH c AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM departments)
SELECT name FROM c WHERE id = 4; -- Q56 MATERIALIZED runs CTE once; NOT MATERIALIZED inlines

caption.text:
60 SQL queries to crack any data interview 🎯

I wrote out sixty solved drills on PostgreSQL by hand. Every one shows the task, the solution code and the exact result, so you can check your own output line by line.

They all run on one employees / departments / orders schema, ordered from easy to hard:

1️⃣ The Practice Schema
2️⃣ Basics and Filtering
3️⃣ Aggregates, GROUP BY and HAVING
4️⃣ Joins
5️⃣ Subqueries
6️⃣ Window Functions
7️⃣ CTEs
8️⃣ Real Interview Scenarios
9️⃣ SQL Cheatsheet

Start at the top and work down. By the interview scenarios, the patterns will feel familiar.

Swipe through, try each query before you look at the answer, and save this for your next prep session. 📌

Comment “sql” to get every query and answer as a PDF.
